herodotus.author: Herodotus
herodotus.note: main narrative; wrote about 50 years after the battle, from Athenian and other informants

facts.claim: The battle of Salamis was fought in 480 BC, traditionally dated to late September.
The envoys returned as suppliants carrying olive branches and were given a second answer: Zeus grants that a wooden wall alone shall not be taken.
Some older Athenians believed the wooden wall meant the thorn hedge that once ringed the Acropolis.
The Athenians evacuated their families and slaves to Troezen, Aegina and Salamis.
A few Athenians, the temple stewards and poor men, stayed on the Acropolis behind a barricade of planks and timber, believing it was the wooden wall of the oracle.
The Persians climbed the steep front of the Acropolis near the shrine of Aglauros, where no guard was posted.
They killed the defenders, plundered the temple and set the whole Acropolis on fire.
Xerxes sent a horseman to Susa to announce his success.

facts.note: A story the Athenians told Herodotus; say 'Herodotus says' or 'the Athenians said'.
facts.claim: Herodotus says Athena's sacred olive tree burned with the temple, yet the next day a new shoot a cubit long had grown from the stump.
When news reached the Greek fleet at Salamis that the Acropolis had fallen, some commanders panicked and voted to sail away to the Isthmus.
Athens supplied the largest contingent of the Greek fleet: 180 ships.
